connections.why: Open monitoring notices what attention is doing, including now.

connections.title: Learn to redirect attention after distraction — the return, not the absence of distraction, is the skill
connections.why: The return is the skill; this is one of them.

prompts.text: What are you avoiding by staying busy — and what would you find if you stopped?

connections.title: Scheduled empty time
connections.why: Empty time is where what you're avoiding shows up.

connections.title: Value silence
connections.why: Silence is what busyness is keeping at bay.

prompts.text: What would you do if you weren't afraid of looking foolish — and is the fear the only thing in the way?

connections.title: Practice shame (aidos)
connections.why: Aidos is the right amount of shame; too much is cowardice in costume.

connections.title: Understand fear's function — it prepares you for threat
connections.why: Fear's job is preparation, not paralysis.

prompts.text: What is the return you owe — and would a like-for-like exchange actually be fitting?

connections.title: Practise reciprocity (antapodosis)
connections.why: A return is matched to what was given, not identical.

connections.title: Practice generosity (eleutheriotes)
connections.why: Right giving includes the right return.

prompts.text: What is something an experienced person in your life sees that you don't yet?

connections.title: Practise perceptiveness (aisthesis)
connections.why: Aristotle says experience gives the eye.

connections.title: Cultivate practical judgment (gnome)
connections.why: Gnome comes with age and use.

prompts.text: What is the smallest good thing in the room right now?

connections.title: Five-senses grounding
connections.why: Grounding is attention to what's actually here.

connections.title: Make eudaimonia the organising end of your life
connections.why: Eudaimonia is the pattern small goods add up to.

prompts.text: What are you deliberating about that you've already decided?

connections.title: Deliberate well
connections.why: Aristotle says the doctor asks how, never whether.

connections.title: Set right intention
connections.why: The aim behind the act, once set, ends the weighing.

prompts.text: What is the quality you've repeated into being that you'd keep — and one you'd change?

connections.title: Recognise that virtue is a hexis, not a feeling
connections.why: A hexis is formed by repetition.

connections.title: Understand that you are responsible for your character
connections.why: The repetition is still partly yours to steer.

prompts.text: Which friendship would survive a change in circumstance — and which wouldn't?

connections.title: Recognise that friendships change over time
connections.why: The floor is the circumstance; when it goes, some friendships go.

connections.title: Know the three kinds of friendship
connections.why: The character kind is the one that survives.

prompts.text: What is the pleasure that costs more than it gives?

connections.title: Practise moderation in pleasure
connections.why: Aristotle says excess marks the bad man, not the pleasure.

connections.title: Practice temperance (sophrosyne)
connections.why: Temperance is appetite's order; disorder is the cost.

prompts.text: What is the thing you can't rehearse for — and how are you preparing anyway?

connections.title: Handle anxiety by returning to the present
connections.why: The return is the preparation.

connections.title: Practice creative hopelessness — let go of what isn't working
connections.why: Creative hopelessness is the discovery that avoidance is what isn't working.

prompts.text: What is the pain you've stopped trying to fix — and what does sitting with it teach?

connections.title: Radical acceptance
connections.why: Radical acceptance is the sitting-with, not the approving-of.

connections.title: Practice resilience in adversity
connections.why: Aristotle distinguishes bearing misfortune from not feeling it.

prompts.text: What is the difference between your smartest opinion and your truest one?

connections.title: Practise the unity of the virtues
connections.why: If the virtues are unified, the smartest opinion without the good is a partial virtue at best.

connections.title: Practice truthfulness (aletheia)
connections.why: Truthfulness includes the opinions you'd rather not defend.
